section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section contains the opening header and date of the maamar.
section.t: With the help of Heaven.
The night before Tuesday,
the tenth of Kislev, 5741*

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that "He redeemed my soul in peace" refers to a redemption where the opponent is completely nullified without war, as in the days of Shlomo, with ultimate perfection in the future era.
section.t: "He redeemed my soul in peace from the battle against me, for many were with me."
And the master of the redemption explains in his discourse beginning with these words
(which was printed in his book Shaarei Teshuvah),
that the interpretation of "He redeemed in peace"
(specifically "in peace")
is that the redemption is in a manner that the opponent is completely nullified,
so that there is no need for any war at all.
And this is analogous to what was in the days of Shlomo,
that all the nations were nullified before Shlomo,
not through war,
therefore he was called Shlomo because there was peace in his days, etc.
However, the peace in the days of Shlomo was not yet complete,
and the ultimate perfection of this will be in the days of Moshiach, when evil will be completely nullified
(as it is stated,
"And the spirit of impurity I will remove from the earth"),
therefore then "all the nations will flow to him," etc.
(and they will flow of their own accord),
and likewise regarding animals—"they will neither harm nor destroy," etc.
"And the lion shall eat straw like the ox,"
and one could perhaps say,
that from the fact that the discourse brings the verse "and the lion shall eat straw like the ox,"
it is understood
that within the days of Moshiach themselves,
the perfection of "He redeemed in peace" will be specifically in the second period.
And as explained elsewhere
the mediation of opinions
in the interpretation of "And the wolf shall dwell with the lamb," etc.,
that in the first period of the days of Moshiach this will be in the manner of "a parable and riddle,"
referring to the nations of the world,
and in the second period it will be literal
(regarding animals).

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the redemption in peace achieved through Torah study is a clarification that nullifies evil inherently, unlike prayer which involves a struggle.
section.t: B)
And the explanation of the matter
(that although the concept of redemption in peace also existed in the days of Shlomo,
nevertheless,
the ultimate perfection of this will be in the days of Moshiach,
and within them specifically in the second period),
will be understood from what is explained in the discourse,
that also through engaging in Torah study
(now)
a redemption in peace is effected,
because the clarification accomplished through engaging in Torah is "a level of nullifying evil in its very essence."
And as explained in several discourses
the difference between Torah and prayer,
that the clarification of prayer is in the manner of war,
"the time of prayer is a time of battle,"
and the clarification of Torah is in the manner of rest.

For the difference between clarification through war and clarification through rest is that in clarification through war, the clarifier must clothe himself in the garments of that which is being clarified,
but not so in clarification through rest,
the clarifier remains in his place,
and through the revelation of the light
(of the clarifier)
that shines upon that which is being clarified,
it becomes clarified automatically.
And as it was in the days of Shlomo,
that Shlomo was in his place,
and through the greatness of his name that was heard even in distant places,
they were drawn to him of their own accord,
as it is stated,
"And the queen of Sheba heard the fame of Shlomo... and she came to Jerusalem."
For likewise is the difference between the clarification of prayer and the clarification of Torah,
that the clarification of prayer is in a manner that the Nefesh HaElokis clothes itself in the Nefesh HaBahamis
(and as is known,
that in order for the contemplation of prayer to effect a clarification of the Nefesh HaBahamis,
the contemplation must be on such matters and in such a manner that the Nefesh HaBahamis can also grasp them),
but not so the clarification of Torah, which is in a manner of automatic effect,
for by learning in Torah that this thing is permitted and this thing is forbidden,
they become clarified automatically.
